basis: Developmental delay is obligate. Clinodactyly (30-79%) and dermatoglyphic variation do not establish functional damage; significant skeletal and cardiac defects are occasional.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent clinodactyly is a minor skeletal variant without established functional damage; other skeletal lesions occur in <30%.

basis: Polymicrogyria defines disease; vascular/valvular defects, abnormal scarring and clubfeet occur in 1/1 annotated case. Sparse evidence; gingival recession omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: vascular EDS is optional, while vascular/valvular abnormalities occur in 1/1 annotated case; not defining across the whole concept.

basis: Cutis laxa defines disease; joint laxity 4/4 with skeletal deformities, GI diverticula 2/2, high myopia 3/4 and ectropion 3/3. Bladder diverticula 3/4 omitted at cap; small cohorts.

decisions.renal: none under cap: bladder diverticula affect 3/4; retain widespread skeletal disease, GI wall defects/prolapse and ocular dysfunction.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: gastric and colonic diverticula each occur in 2/2 assessed patients, with rectal prolapse also documented; direct visceral connective-tissue disease.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint hypermobility 4/4, pectus deformity 3/4 and scoliosis 2/4 establish common skeletal involvement; skin laxity defines the disease.

basis: Inherited phosphate disorder with defining periarticular/tendon calcinosis and skeletal disease. Cerebral calcification in 1/1 lacks demonstrated neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: periarticular/tendon calcinosis is the defining lesion, supported by Achilles calcification and skeletal abnormalities in 1/1.

basis: Immune dysregulation with cytopenias 46-85%; endocrine pancreatic autoimmunity 4/5 and enteropathy/exocrine failure 38-40%. Dermatitis 2/5 omitted at cap; pneumonitis 3/13 below threshold.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: endocrine pancreatic autoimmunity occurs in 4/5 annotated patients as direct multisystem disease; endocrine disease does not define the whole syndrome.

basis: Glycosylation disorder with defining CNS and skeletal disease; hydroureter 3/4, nephrocalcinosis 30-79%. Ocular findings 4/4, hearing and heart defects 30-79% omitted at cap; visual loss is cerebral.

decisions.renal: involved: hydroureter affects 3/4 and nephrocalcinosis 30-79%; intrinsic urinary structural disease takes the remaining slot.
decisions.ocular: none under cap: cerebral visual impairment belongs to neurologic; hypermetropia/strabismus 4/4 are less severe than the retained urinary structural disease.

basis: Complex I disorder defined by cardiomyopathy (4/4) and neurologic dysfunction (encephalopathy 3/4); hepatic steatosis 30-79%. Common myopathy/cytopenias omitted at cap; acute liver failure <30%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic steatosis occurs in 30-79%; liver failure is explicitly characteristic, supporting hepatic priority under the four-axis cap.
decisions.neurologic: primary: neurological dysfunction is explicit in the definition and encephalopathy occurs in 3/4 patients.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none under cap: direct myopathy occurs in 30-79%, but defining cardiac/CNS disease and hepatic involvement take priority.

basis: FKRP dystroglycan glycosylation disorder causes muscular dystrophy; cardiomyopathy affects roughly 30-50% in predominant limb-girdle disease. Brain/eye defects characterize severe minority subtypes.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: cardiomyopathy affects roughly 30-50% of the predominant FKRP limb-girdle phenotype and reflects direct myocardial dystroglycan dysfunction.

basis: Chronic inflammation of gingiva defines the disease. Plaque association alone does not establish an infectious or autoimmune diagnosis for this broad concept.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: local gingival inflammation, commonly plaque-associated, does not itself establish infection, immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease.

basis: Joubert CNS malformation with defining ocular phenotype through its ocular-defect parent; AHI1-associated retinal dystrophy occurs in roughly 70-80%. Renal disease is a minority manifestation.

decisions.ocular: primary: the supplied parent is Joubert syndrome with ocular defect; characteristic retinal dystrophy affects roughly 70-80% and is intrinsic eye disease.
